Hi Thomas — thanks for the clear checklist and timeline. Looping in Aditya (network infra) and Jonas (private deployment ops) for the technical details.

Short answers up front:
- We support both models: (A) per-customer reserved, static egress IPs (customer-assigned elastic addresses) and (B) Redwood-managed NAT pool with ephemeral binding.
- We can provide an evidence pack (IP allocation receipts, ASN ownership, and routing prefix declarations) for reservation-mode deployments; ephemeral pools include rotation windows and a signed rotation manifest for audits.
- Common TLS/DNS patterns: runtime outbound connections use SNI that matches the downstream service hostname; we also make optional ALPN recommendations for mutual TLS. If you have egress TLS-inspection in place, SNI allowlisting is typically sufficient but full TLS break-and-inspect will require a short list of CA fingerprints/rotation expectations.

I'll attach an options matrix that maps the tradeoffs (egress_options_matrix.xlsx). Can the EdgeCorp security team confirm which model they prefer? If you pick reserved IPs we will request the target elastic IPs from your cloud account or coordinate allocation if you prefer Redwood to provision on your behalf.

Operational notes (high level):
- Reserved IPs: lowest friction for firewall teams; requires static binding and will not rotate without scheduled maintenance.
- Ephemeral NAT pool: lower cost and easier infra ops on our side; requires a migration window for rotation (we provide a signed rotation manifest 48 hours before rotation).
- Fallback: if outbound traffic is blocked, we support a 'controlplane-proxy' fallback where limited telemetry/health egress goes via a hosted control-plane endpoint (only used during onboarding/failover).

Next steps proposed:
1) EdgeCorp confirms model preference.
2) Redwood provides IP evidence pack or rotation SLAs.
3) Align on a maintenance window for any planned IP changes.

Olga
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context — quick technical appendix below to help EdgeCorp pick: 

Option 1 — Reserved per-tenant IPs (recommended for strict allowlists)
- Mechanism: customer provides/allocates X elastic IPs in their VPC and maps them to our private endpoint NAT gateway during provisioning; IPs are associated with the tenant's NAT gateway and do not rotate unless requested.
- Pros: simple allowlist, straightforward audit evidence, predictable connectivity.
- Cons: extra customer cloud quota and potential cost for reserved addresses.

Option 2 — Redwood-managed gated NAT pool (recommended for scale & multi-customer)
- Mechanism: Redwood manages a pool of egress IPs and binds them to tenants via session NAT; we publish a 72-hour rotation manifest and a 48-hour push notification before changes.
- Pros: no customer-reserved addresses needed; easier to scale.
- Cons: requires your firewall to accept short-lived changes or to allow a set of fallback IPs.

Option 3 — Customer-edge proxy (most locked-down)
- Mechanism: traffic never leaves customer VPC to Redwood egress; instead, runtime calls the customer's outbound proxy which performs calls to downstream services.
- Pros: customer controls all egress; easy for inspection/logging.
- Cons: places operational burden on customer and can increase latency.

TLS/SNI notes:
- Our runtime uses SNI consistent with destination hostnames. If you have SNI-based allowlisting, include the destination FQDNs in the allowlist (we will provide the list).
- If you perform TLS interception, you will see short-lived certs from our side; we can provide expected CA fingerprints and a rotation cadence for audit.

Operational SLAs and evidence we can provide:
- IP ownership receipts (ARIN/RIPE entries), signed rotation manifests, packet-capture snippets (redacted) for onboarding tests, and an RFC-style runbook for firewall teams.

I attached a simple diagram (redwood_private_egress_design_v1.png) in the shared drive link for clarity. Happy to run a 30-minute deep-dive with your networking engineers.

- Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
